eras.label: Before 10,000 BCE · Human origins and stone tools
10,000 BCE onwards · Food production and regional cultures

events.title: Palaeolithic tool traditions
events.date_label: c.2.5 million years ago–10,000 BCE · broad chapter scheme
events.summary: Old Stone Age hunting and gathering; broad global teaching range, not a securely dated start for India. Numeric placement of the remote starting point is approximate.

events.title: Early Middle Palaeolithic transition at Attirampakkam
events.summary: Prepared-core/flake transition dated by luminescence; this Indian sequence extends to about 172 thousand years ago. Placement is approximate, not an exact BCE date.

events.title: Homo sapiens evolves in Africa
events.summary: Modern human origins predate the Upper Palaeolithic. Numeric placement is approximate; a tool industry is not a biological species.

events.title: Lower Palaeolithic in the simplified chapter scheme
events.summary: Approximate ending boundary used by the chapter; not a synchronous change across India. Attirampakkam demonstrates much earlier Middle Palaeolithic technology.

events.title: Middle Palaeolithic: conventional teaching range
events.summary: Flake and prepared-core industries. This conventional range does not override earlier securely dated regional evidence.

events.title: Upper Palaeolithic: conventional range
events.summary: Blade–burin toolkits, bone working, ornaments and symbolic expression; regional variation remains.

events.title: Mesolithic: conventional chapter range
events.summary: Microlithic hunting/fishing/gathering communities; regional Mesolithic traditions persisted later than this range.

events.title: Early farming settlement at Mehrgarh
events.summary: Balochistan farming village with wheat/barley, livestock and mud-brick houses; early levels preceded pottery.

events.title: Neolithic: broad chapter range
events.summary: Farming, animal keeping, polished tools and village life developed unevenly.

events.title: Chalcolithic regional villages
events.summary: Copper and stone used together in farming villages; overlaps Harappan Bronze Age urbanism rather than universally preceding it.

events.title: Southern Neolithic agro-pastoral traditions
events.summary: Cattle keeping, ashmounds and ground stone tools characterise several Deccan communities; beginning/end varied locally.

events.title: Ganeshwar–Jodhpura: conventional regional range
events.summary: Rajasthan copper-working sites linked to wider Harappan-period exchange; not a universal beginning date for copper use.

events.title: Mature Harappan civilisation: contextual comparison
events.summary: Bronze Age towns coexisted with regional copper-stone villages. Undeciphered writing places Harappan studies within protohistory.

events.title: Iron Age: broad chapter range
events.summary: Regional iron-using traditions overlapped later Chalcolithic societies; this is not a universal date for the earliest iron.

events.title: Foote recognises a Palaeolithic handaxe at Pallavaram
events.summary: Robert Bruce Foote’s recognised discovery near Chennai opened a major phase of Indian prehistoric research.

events.title: Lubbock publishes Pre-historic Times
events.summary: John Lubbock introduced the Palaeolithic and Neolithic terminology.

events.title: Sankalia identifies the Nevasa flake industry
events.summary: H. D. Sankalia’s Pravara-valley work is associated with identifying the Indian Middle Palaeolithic/Nevasian industry.
